slide1.eyebrow: Integrated Campus Logistics Supply Chain Solution
slide1.title: HORIZONU UNIFORM

box2.title: Core Operational Challenges

slide3.title: Stakeholder Mapping & Physical Cargo Flow
slide3.subtitle: Integrated physical flow from garment vendor to student handoff under the 'Data Locks Physical Asset' doctrine

col1.title: Garment & Shoe Factories
col1.p1: Produces uniform and footwear packages based on aggregate purchase orders (PO).
col1.p2: Enforces strict 5-segment SKU coding standards per category and size.
col1.p3: Cargo Point: Inbound container shipments delivered to campus warehouse (Inbound Logistics).

col2.title: Campus Logistics Warehouse
col2.p1: Physical cargo receiving (StockReceive) and quality control (QC).
col2.p2: Strict FIFO (First-In, First-Out) batch recording and landed unit cost assignment.
col2.p3: Cargo Point: Outbound transfer of oldest batches to distribution booths.

col3.title: Finance & On-Site Booth Staff
col3.p1: Finance: Authorizes student tuition payment status (Eligibility verification).
col3.p2: Booth Staff: Serves physical garment distribution at campus pickup booths.
col3.p3: Critical Point: QR Code identity scanning and size fitting validation.

col4.title: Freshman Students (Customers)
col4.p1: End consumers with official package entitlements per study program.
col4.p2: Submits body size profiles via student portal and receives assigned schedule tickets.
col4.p3: Info Point: Presents high-resolution QR Code ticket (student ID) at pickup booth.
col4.flow: Flow: Size Profile ➔ Tailored Uniform Package

slide4.title: Operational Bottlenecks & Systemic Impact Evaluation
slide4.subtitle: Comprehensive root cause analysis of manual spreadsheets causing cost overruns, delays, and service degradation
slide4.thImpact: Impact on Cost, Time, Inventory & Service

row1.cause: Factory procurement orders were based purely on historical heuristic ratios. No pre-enrollment self-service size survey existed prior to vendor contract tenders.
row1.impact: Inventory & Cost Impact: Popular sizes (M/L) depleted on day one, while extreme sizes (XS, 3XL) gathered dust for years. University working capital locked in dead-stock.

row2.cause: Finance managed a massive spreadsheet file (~4.5 MB, 19 sheets) for thousands of students. Pickup appointment slots were distributed via manual email blasts.
row2.impact: Time & Service Impact: Constant software freezes and data corruption risks. Data reconciliation consumed weeks and distribution schedules reached students late.

row3.cause: Tuition clearance verification, academic entitlement matching, and physical handover confirmations were handled manually by paper checklist tick marks.
row3.impact: Time & Accuracy Impact: Service times lagged at 15–20 minutes per student with hundred-meter queues, leaving high exposure to duplicate claims across different booths or days.

row4.cause: Uniform receipts from vendors with fluctuating prices were not tracked via FIFO queues or automated ledger entries tied to booth POS handovers.
row4.impact: Cost & Audit Impact: Unaccounted inventory shrinkage without audit trails. Real-time Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) and Gross Profit Margin (GPM) calculations were severely distorted.

slide5.title: Data Bottlenecks & Information Silos (As-Is State)
slide5.subtitle: Inter-departmental communication barriers triggering service delays, data inconsistencies, and transaction friction

card1.title: Requirement: Size Profiles & Schedules
card1.p1: Source & Target: Students submit data to campus; receive schedule via email.
card1.p2: Pain Point: Disconnected Google Forms without standardized SKU validation, resulting in duplicate entries and manual staff consolidation delays of 2–3 weeks.

card2.title: Requirement: Tuition Paid Status (Eligibility)
card2.p1: Source & Target: Finance exports paid clearance status to booth staff.
card2.p2: Pain Point: Static local Excel exports. Day-of bank clearing updates fail to reach booth stations in real time, causing paid students to be wrongly turned away.

card3.title: Requirement: Package Entitlement & Stock Ledger
card3.p1: Source & Target: Booth staff verifies entitlements and logs item release.
card3.p2: Pain Point: Physical logbooks tallying handovers. Warehouse stock balances were only reconciled at night, leaving large gaps for shrinkage and stock discrepancies.

card4.title: Requirement: Aggregate Purchase Orders (PO)
card4.p1: Source & Target: Procurement dispatches garment production quantities to vendor.
card4.p2: Pain Point: Purchase orders drafted from crude estimates rather than validated student anthropometric demand, triggering multi-month return-exchange lead times.
card4.status: Status: Blind Ordering (Lack of Real Demand Signal)

slide6.title: Information System Architecture Selection (HorizonU Uniform Engine)
slide6.subtitle: Unified convergence of four enterprise pillars: ERP, SCM, POS, and WMS in a modern web platform

row1.func: Governs student master data, 4-segment base SKU hierarchy, bulk excel imports via background jobs, and automated academic entitlement matrix per program.
row1.benefit: 100% Crash-Free: Full ACID transaction integrity with unified single source of truth.

row2.func: Opens pre-enrollment self-service size selection windows (SizeChangeEvent), program-filtered slot broadcasts, and automated Demand vs. Shortage calculus for procurement tenders.
row2.benefit: Zero Dead-Stock: Factory purchase orders match 100% of verified student physical measurements.

row3.func: Issues tamper-proof Level-H QR code passes and executes 6-tier atomic validation on scanner read (Payment, Time Slot, Program, Gender, Entitlement Balance, Rack Stock).
row3.benefit: Service Time < 30s: Instant validation with zero duplicate claim vulnerability.

row4.func: Tracks oldest vendor intake batches (FIFO), ledger-backed stock deductions, physical Stock Opname variance audits, and real-time gross margin profit analytics.
row4.benefit: Real-Time FIFO Valuation: Transparent audit trails and elimination of physical discrepancies.

slide7.title: 4-Phase Closed-Loop Supply Chain Architecture
slide7.subtitle: End-to-end system connectivity, atomic transaction processing, and closed-loop data feedback

phase1.title: Inbound & FIFO Batch Registry
phase1.p1: • Logs bulk cargo shipments from apparel suppliers via StockReceive module.
phase1.p2: • Assigns sequential FIFO batch tracking IDs (First-In, First-Out sequence).
phase1.p3: • Automatically posts inventory journal inflows (StockMovement IN) and fixes batch cost basis.

phase2.title: Eligibility Clearance & Size Profiling
phase2.p1: • Finance authorizes enrolled students in EligibilityRecord table.
phase2.p2: • Freshmen log in to self-submit body size measurements through student portal.
phase2.p3: • System aggregates Demand vs. Shortage analytics to drive supplier procurement contracts.
phase2.output: Output: Active QR Pass & Assigned Time Slot

phase3.title: POS QR & 6-Tier Atomic Validation
phase3.p1: • Booth staff scans student QR code using webcam-based scanner client.
phase3.p2: • Executes 6-tier atomic validation under pessimistic database row locking (lockForUpdate).
phase3.p3: • Automatically depletes oldest FIFO batches (deductStockFifo) and prints handover receipt.

phase4.title: Stock Opname & Closed-Loop Feedback
phase4.p1: • Periodic physical stock audit with automated discrepancy variance calculation.
phase4.p2: • Generates shrinkage/surplus adjustment journal vouchers instantly.
phase4.p3: • Produces executive Gross Profit Margin (GPM) dashboards and dead-stock alerts for management.

slide8.title: Implementation Priorities & Field Risk Mitigation
slide8.subtitle: Operational readiness roadmap alongside battle-tested contingency protocols for distribution day

priorities.title: System Readiness Roadmap
priorities.p1: • Priority 1 (Master Data): Cleanse legacy records, deploy 5-segment SKU schema, import student cohorts, and configure program entitlement rules.
priorities.p2: • Priority 2 (Portal Integration): Bridge live tuition clearance feeds (Eligibility), launch self-service size survey portal, and broadcast assigned schedule slots.
priorities.p3: • Priority 3 (Human Readiness): Conduct operational drills for booth staff on webcam scanners, size exchange SOPs, and offline fallback procedures.

slide1.html:
OPENING"Good morning/afternoon, Distinguished Judges of Technospark and respected audience. We are from the Nirwana Team, consisting of Fhazar, Ferry, Hildan, Fadel, Daffa, and Acep. Today, we are proud to present an integrated supply chain information system solution entitled: HorizonU Uniform.

Our case study focuses on the Finance Department of Horizon University Indonesia, which is responsible for the annual procurement and distribution of thousands of uniform packages, blazers, lab shoes, and medical kits for incoming freshmen.

Before HorizonU Uniform was developed, operations relied on a massive 4.5 MB master Excel spreadsheet across 19 worksheets that frequently froze and crashed. In the field, students waited 15–20 minutes in line, size mismatches created massive dead-stock, and duplicate claims were a constant risk. Let us examine how this supply chain operates."

slide3.html:
SCM STRUCTURE"Moving to Slide 3 regarding Supply Chain Structure. The HorizonU Uniform supply chain bridges four key stakeholders:"

"1. Suppliers (Upstream): Garment and footwear factories manufacturing items based on university procurement orders.
2. Campus Warehouse (Inbound): Inspects incoming shipments (QC) and registers batches under strict FIFO rules.
3. Finance & Booth Staff (Verifiers): Finance verifies tuition clearance (Eligibility), while booth teams scan QR codes for physical handover.
4. Students (Downstream): The end consumers who submit size measurements online and present digital passes at pickup stations."

"All four entities operate under one core rule: 'Data Locks Physical Asset'—no goods leave without real-time digital verification."

slide4.html:
PROBLEM ANALYSIS"On Slide 4, we examine the four primary root causes and their systemic impacts:"

"First, Size Mismatches: Factory orders based on heuristic estimates meant popular sizes ran out on day one while extreme sizes accumulated for years as dead-stock.
Second, Spreadsheet Crashes: Managing 4.5 MB Excel workbooks for thousands of students caused software freezes and delayed schedules.
Third, Booth Queuing: Manual paper checklists led to 15–20 minute turnaround times per student and high double-claim exposure.
Fourth, Opaque Costs: Inventory lacked FIFO batch tracking, obscuring real-time COGS and auditability."

"These challenges prove that manual spreadsheets are incapable of scaling for modern campus operations."

slide5.html:
INFORMATION FLOW"Next on Slide 5, we map the As-Is Information Flow and its communication bottlenecks:"

"Flow 1 (Student to Campus): Unstandardized Google Forms created duplicate entries and prolonged data cleanup by weeks.
Flow 2 (Finance to Booths): Local Excel files created data silos; day-of bank clearances failed to reach booth staff in real time.
Flow 3 (Booths to Warehouse): Paper logs reconciled only at night left open windows for inventory shrinkage.
Flow 4 (Procurement to Factory): Blind ordering without verified student demand resulted in multi-month exchange cycles."

"The solution requires centralizing all four data streams into a single real-time transactional platform."

slide6.html:
RECOMMENDED SYSTEMS"To resolve these bottlenecks, on Slide 6 we recommend four integrated enterprise pillars:"

"1. ERP Master & Entitlement Engine: Enforces 5-segment SKU standards and automatic academic entitlement matrices under MySQL InnoDB ACID compliance.
2. SCM Demand Planning Portal: Provides self-service size survey events and broadcasts schedule slots, achieving Zero Dead-Stock.
3. POS QR Verification Engine: High-density QR code scanning with 6-tier atomic checks cuts service time to under 30 seconds per student.
4. WMS & FIFO Costing Engine: Automatically pulls oldest inventory batches and records movement ledgers for 100% transparent audit trails."

"Together, these modules form an enterprise-grade platform specifically designed for campus logistics."

ARCHITECTURE DESIGN"On Slide 7, we present the 4-Phase Closed-Loop Architecture:"

"Phase 1 (Inbound): Vendor shipments recorded in StockReceive with sequential FIFO batch IDs and landed cost entries.
Phase 2 (Demand): Finance activates cleared students; students submit body measurements; Demand vs. Shortage calculus drives procurement.
Phase 3 (Outbound): Booth scanning triggers 6-tier atomic validation under pessimistic database row locking (lockForUpdate).
Phase 4 (Audit & Control): Periodic physical stock audits generate variance journals and real-time gross margin analytics."

"This closed loop guarantees end-to-end data integrity from factory intake to student handoff."

IMPLEMENTATION & RISKS"Moving to Slide 8 on Implementation Priorities and Field Risk Mitigation."

"We structure deployment into 3 core priorities: Master Data setup in Weeks 1–2, Portal Integration in Weeks 3–4, and Staff Drills in Weeks 5–6.

For field contingency, we prepare 3 resilience protocols:
• Dead Student Phone: Instant fallback search by Student ID or Name.
• Size Stockout: Partial Pickup dispenses available items without voiding remaining balances.
• Network Latency: Pessimistic row locking ensures zero double deductions."

"With these SOPs, the university maintains uninterrupted operations under peak pressure."
